Reproducibility

How the fictional data were generated

The script creates both with-tool and without-tool outcomes for each fictional team, then reveals only the outcome under the assigned status to the analyst. Separate mini-rollout and advertising experiments illustrate random assignment.

Fixed seed: 7107. Read the complete generator and analysis code; inspect the saved results.

Known truth: The generator stores both potential outcomes. Its average effect among recipients is 4.58; its average effect across all teams is 2.42. Those are different targets.

These are model assumptions and generated outcomes, not claims about a real population.

Stop 01 / 24

Will changing the action change the outcome?

A forecasting model asks which teams will finish more work. A causal question asks how the same teams would perform under a specified alternative. Those questions need different comparisons. High-performing teams might adopt a tool more often even if the tool does nothing; a useful intervention might also be targeted at teams starting behind.

This lesson moves from a fully visible synthetic world to a simulated advertising experiment where only assigned outcomes are observed. In both cases the object is a difference between interventions, not a label attached to a correlation.

Pause and explain

A tool predicts performance well. Does that establish the value of deploying it?

Compare your reasoning

No. Prediction can exploit selection, baseline ability, or consequences of treatment. Deployment requires a comparison of potential outcomes under the deployment policy.

Stop 02 / 24

Open the teaching world before analyzing it

The lab uses NumPy seed 7107. It draws skill from {0,1,2,3}, load from {0,1,2}, and independent normal baseline noise with standard deviation 2. The units are fictional teams, and the outcome is an arbitrary weekly production index. Every parameter is an invented teaching assumption, not an empirical estimate.

Yᵢ(0) = 40 + 4 skillᵢ − 2 loadᵢ + εᵢ; τᵢ = 2 + 1.5 skillᵢ − 2 loadᵢ; Yᵢ(1) = Yᵢ(0) + τᵢ.

The initial adoption rule is D = 1 when skill is at least 2. This deliberate selection creates a visible distinction between treatment effects and baseline differences. Download the script to change the rule while keeping the potential outcomes fixed.

Stop 03 / 24

Make “adopt the tool” operational

Define treatment as enabling one specified scheduling tool, with the same onboarding and support, for one week. Define control as retaining the existing process over that week. Keep eligibility, outcome measurement and the follow-up window common to both groups. If onboarding changes too, the treatment is the package, not the software alone.

A precise treatment does not hold every consequence fixed. If the tool changes coordination time and that changes production, coordination is part of the total effect. Adjusting for it would change the question.

Pause and explain

Would comparing enthusiastic adopters with teams never offered the tool estimate the offer effect?

Compare your reasoning

Not automatically. Adoption reflects behavior after an offer, while assignment to an offer is a different intervention. Define which policy is being evaluated before estimating it.

Stop 05 / 24

Use the switching equation in the right direction

Yᵢ = DᵢYᵢ(1) + (1 − Dᵢ)Yᵢ(0).

For team 1, D = 1, so its observed value is 56.62. Its other potential outcome is not observed by that assignment. The equation selects an outcome; it does not recover the missing one.

A before–after measurement is a different time point, not the same team’s untreated outcome at the post-treatment date. Secular demand, learning and changing staffing can move outcomes even without adoption.

Pause and explain

If D = 0, is the individual treatment effect zero?

Compare your reasoning

No. D = 0 tells us which potential outcome is observed. It says nothing about the unobserved difference Y(1) − Y(0).

Stop 06 / 24

Missing by design is not missing at random in a spreadsheet

Random assignment can identify an average effect without identifying any individual effect. The missingness is fundamental: the same unit cannot simultaneously receive both treatment versions at the same time. Filling in a missing counterfactual from a similar team is an estimator with assumptions, not a recovered observation.

Separate identification from estimation. Identification asks whether the distribution of observed data plus defended assumptions determines the target. Estimation asks how to approximate that target from a finite sample. A very precise estimator cannot repair an unidentified contrast.

The generated effect varies with both skill and load. A high baseline outcome need not imply a high gain. Likewise, an average near zero could conceal beneficial and harmful individual changes. Heterogeneity should be defined in the effect, not inferred from variation in treated outcomes alone.

Pause and explain

Which quantity would rank teams by benefit if both potential outcomes were known?

Compare your reasoning

Rank Y(1) − Y(0), not Y(1). In observational practice those individual differences are unavailable, so policy targeting needs additional modeling, validation and uncertainty.

Stop 08 / 24

ATE, ATT and ATU are different population choices

ATE = E[Y(1) − Y(0)]; ATT = E[Y(1) − Y(0) | D = 1]; ATU = E[Y(1) − Y(0) | D = 0].
Three finite-population average effects
TargetSynthetic truth
ATE2.417
ATT4.583
ATU0.250

With treated share p = 0.500, ATE = p × ATT + (1 − p) × ATU = 2.417. ATT describes selected adopters. It does not automatically answer what would happen when extending the tool to current nonadopters.

Pause and explain

When can ATT equal ATE despite nonrandom adoption?

Compare your reasoning

For example, if treatment effects are constant, or if selection is unrelated to effect heterogeneity. Equality of these targets does not itself remove baseline selection bias in the observed outcome gap.

Stop 09 / 24

Compute the observed gap before calling it causal

The observed treated-minus-untreated mean difference is 15.083 points. This is a correct descriptive contrast, but it compares different teams under different interventions. The synthetic ATE is 2.417; the gap need not estimate it.

Keep subtraction direction explicit. A positive treated-minus-control difference means treated outcomes are higher, not necessarily that treatment raises outcomes. Changing the order changes the sign, not the underlying evidence.

Stop 10 / 24

Separate recipients’ effect from baseline selection

E[Y | D=1] − E[Y | D=0] = ATT + {E[Y(0) | D=1] − E[Y(0) | D=0]}.

Here 15.083 = 4.583 + 10.500. The final term compares both groups under no treatment, not their observed pre-period levels. We can calculate it exactly only because the generator supplies both worlds.

Bias must be stated relative to a target. Subtracting ATT from the raw gap leaves the baseline selection term. Subtracting ATE also brings in the difference between recipients’ effects and everyone’s effects.

Pause and explain

If baseline selection is zero, does the observed difference necessarily equal ATE?

Compare your reasoning

It equals ATT under consistency. To equal ATE as well, ATT must equal ATE, for example through full random assignment or effect homogeneity.

Stop 11 / 24

Comparability is an assignment claim

(Y(0), Y(1)) ⟂ D ⇒ E[Y | D=1] − E[Y | D=0] = ATE.

Independence of assignment from both potential outcomes is stronger than equality of one baseline mean. Randomization provides a design-based reason for independence before outcomes are seen. Observational adjustment instead requires a credible argument that measured pre-treatment variables remove all common causes.

An outside vendor, policy change or administrative rule is not automatically exogenous. Ask whether its timing and allocation depend on expected outcomes. The word “external” is not an identification proof.

Stop 12 / 24

Keep versions, interference and overlap visible

Consistency: the observed outcome corresponds to the intervention specified. No interference: one team’s outcome is not changed by another team’s assignment. Positivity: each target type has a chance of receiving each intervention. These are separate from exchangeability.

If tool users share recommendations with controls, the experiment may estimate a diluted assignment-policy effect. If all high-load teams must receive the tool, their untreated comparison is absent. Neither problem is fixed by a smaller regression p-value.

Pause and explain

Would a random rule solve ambiguous treatment versions?

Compare your reasoning

No. Randomization can balance assignment while the treatment itself remains ill-defined. Document the version, support, exposure and spillover boundary.

Stop 13 / 24

Randomize assignment, not potential outcomes

Complete randomization selects a fixed number of treated teams uniformly from all allowable assignments. The teams and their potential outcomes remain fixed. Only the treatment labels move. Over assignments, the average treated baseline equals the average control baseline, even though any one rollout can be imbalanced.

This is the key design-based distinction: unbiasedness is an average over hypothetical assignments, not a promise that one realized estimate equals the finite-population effect. Random sampling is a separate mechanism governing who enters the experiment.

Pause and explain

Does choosing the assignment with the largest estimated effect preserve this argument?

Compare your reasoning

No. Selecting after seeing outcomes changes the assignment or analysis mechanism and creates selection bias. Prespecified covariate-constrained randomization is different and requires inference matching that design.

Stop 15 / 24

Evidence of randomization lives in the process

Retain the eligibility list, allocation code, random seed, assignment timestamps and exceptions log. Confirm that assignment occurred before exposure and that the implementation respected the recorded labels. Balance tables are useful diagnostics, but a nonsignificant balance test is not proof of randomization.

Do not rerandomize until outcomes or p-values look favorable. If balance restrictions are part of the protocol, use baseline variables and specify them before treatment. Analyze all randomized units according to their original assignment unless a different estimand and valid identification strategy were prespecified.

Stop 16 / 24

Choose a stable unit and analyze that design

An ad impression is not necessarily an independent experiment. The same person can appear many times, see both versions, or influence another person. Assign at the user, household, store or region level that fits the intervention, and measure outcomes over a common follow-up window.

Clustering changes both the causal exposure and the effective information. Thousands of impressions within a few randomized regions do not create thousands of independent assignment units. Plan sample size using the assignment units and likely within-cluster correlation.

Pause and explain

Why not randomize each page load when purchases are user-level?

Compare your reasoning

Repeated users can cross treatments, carry exposure across sessions, and contribute dependent outcomes. Stable user assignment better defines the intervention and denominator for a user-level outcome.

Stop 17 / 24

Assignment and receipt can diverge

A separate encouragement simulation assigns offers at random and lets uptake depend on the offer. The observed first stage is 0.537; the intention-to-treat outcome effect is 2.029. Their ratio is 3.778.

Wald ratio = {E[Y | Z=1] − E[Y | Z=0]} / {E[D | Z=1] − E[D | Z=0]}.

Under random encouragement, relevance, exclusion, monotonicity and suitable consistency/no-interference assumptions, this ratio identifies a complier average effect, not generally ATE. The generator’s receipt effect is 4 and offers have no direct effect, so those assumptions are built in here. In real work they need a substantive defense.

Pause and explain

May we compare recipients with nonrecipients and call that randomized?

Compare your reasoning

No. Receipt is not randomly assigned merely because the offer was. Intention-to-treat retains the random comparison; receipt-effect estimation needs additional assumptions.

Stop 18 / 24

A new advertising experiment with explicit denominators

The next lab generates two independent arms of 12,000 fictional users. Each user receives only one ad version and complete follow-up. A click is Bernoulli with probability 0.065 + 0.009D. An action occurs only after a click, with conditional probability 0.10 − 0.005D. These probabilities are invented design inputs, not facts about advertising.

The generated sample varies around these probabilities. Every estimate below is calculated from the simulated counts, not substituted from the generating expectations.

Stop 19 / 24

A rate answers the question in its denominator

Arm 0 has 8.99% actions per click; arm 1 has 9.91%. Those conditional rates describe selected clickers. If assignment changes who clicks, the clicker populations differ after treatment. They are not automatically a randomized comparison of conversion propensity.

Actions per assigned user = (clicks per assigned user) × (actions per click).

Use actions per assigned user for an assignment-policy effect on actions. Report absolute percentage-point differences before relative lifts. A relative increase can look large when the baseline rate is small.

Pause and explain

Can a version improve click rate but lower actions per click?

Compare your reasoning

Yes. It may attract additional low-intent clickers. Neither metric alone determines the overall actions-per-user effect, which uses the original assigned denominator.

Stop 20 / 24

Quantify uncertainty in the click contrast

SE(p̂₁ − p̂₀) = √{p̂₁(1−p̂₁)/n₁ + p̂₀(1−p̂₀)/n₀}.

The click difference is 1.450 percentage points, or 23.71% relative to arm 0. Its approximate 95% unpooled normal interval is [0.811, 2.089] percentage points. This calculation assumes independent users and the prespecified endpoint.

Click rates by assigned arm — chart data

For rare events or small arms, use an appropriate binomial or randomization-based interval rather than relying automatically on the normal approximation. Repeated peeking and many endpoint searches require a prespecified sequential or multiplicity strategy.

Stop 21 / 24

Keep the downstream endpoint fixed

The action difference is 0.200 percentage points. Its approximate 95% interval is [-0.003, 0.403] percentage points. A click result does not establish an action result, and failure to exclude zero does not establish equivalence.

An equivalence claim needs a substantively meaningful margin and an interval or test designed around it. A decision can still be made under uncertainty, but it should distinguish evidence about the endpoint, estimated economic value, downside risk and the cost of waiting.

Pause and explain

What should “no significant action difference” mean in a report?

Compare your reasoning

The chosen test did not reject its null under its assumptions. Give the estimated difference and interval; do not translate that into proof of zero effect or equal versions.

Stop 22 / 24

With only a treatment indicator, the slope is the gap

Yᵢ = α + βDᵢ + εᵢ; α̂ = mean(Y | D=0), β̂ = mean(Y | D=1) − mean(Y | D=0).

For the binary action outcome, the intercept is 0.00550 and the slope is 0.00200. OLS reproduces the difference in means exactly. The coefficient’s causal interpretation still comes from assignment and the estimand, not from calling the procedure regression.

A Bernoulli outcome is heteroskedastic. Use appropriate robust, design-based or difference-in-proportions uncertainty. Covariate adjustment can improve precision when prespecified baseline covariates are available; a two-row summary does not contain those covariates.

Stop 23 / 24

Translate effects into a decision threshold

In an explicitly hypothetical business scenario, each action contributes 30 currency units and the new version costs 0.02 extra per assigned user. The break-even effect is 0.067 percentage points. Estimated incremental contribution is 0.0400 per user, with the action interval translated to [-0.0210, 0.1010]. This ignores uncertainty in margins and costs.

For a separate fixed-sample planning calculation, detecting an 0.8-percentage-point click difference near a 6.9% pooled rate with 80% power at two-sided 5% significance needs approximately 15,757 users per arm. The simple normal approximation assumes independent observations and no multiplicity. Power for actions must use the action endpoint, not clicks.

Pause and explain

Why compare the interval with a break-even threshold rather than zero alone?

Compare your reasoning

Zero is a scientific reference. The economic threshold includes incremental cost and value. A positive effect can still lose money, and a worthwhile decision can depend on risk and opportunity cost as well as statistical significance.

Stop 24 / 24

Write a bounded causal decision brief

A defensible brief names the intervention, unit, eligible population, endpoint, follow-up period and estimand. It explains assignment and compliance, reports the effect with uncertainty, and distinguishes causal identification from transport to another setting. It states what could change the decision.

For this fictional ad study, the assigned-user comparisons are randomized by construction and users are independent. That makes the simulated contrasts interpretable for the generated population. It supplies no empirical evidence that a real ad version will work. A real rollout would need implementation records, business inputs, uncertainty at the true assignment unit and an explicit follow-up plan.

Pause and explain

What is the strongest transferable lesson from a synthetic experiment?

Compare your reasoning

The reasoning and reproducible analysis workflow transfer. Its numerical effects do not. Design a real comparison whose assumptions and decision threshold can be defended.
